headline: Highest risk is AutoGen’s writable, networked code-execution surface; the pair otherwise has little direct interaction with Whisper’s audio-only, non-networked profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest and act on tool outputs and file contents, while Whisper only processes audio/speech and has no shared channel by default. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not inherent to the pair; it would require an unusual manual handoff or shared workspace. The uncertainty is low because neither profile shows clipboard/MCP bridging.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Whisper transcripts into AutoGen prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file drop that AutoGen reads as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs as plain data, not instructions.
Use a separate folder for Whisper artifacts and mark it read-only for AutoGen.
Add a short prompt prefix telling AutoGen to treat transcripts as untrusted input.
Review any copied transcript before pasting into AutoGen.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Whisper-derived text before AutoGen consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write working directories and has broad network egress, but Whisper has no network egress and only touches audio files. The pair does not show a default shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so leakage is limited unless the operator co-locates sensitive files. Because AutoGen handles model-provider API keys, accidental exposure is possible but not inherent.
conditions: IF sensitive audio transcripts are placed in a directory AutoGen can read, AutoGen may expose them through its outputs or network calls.
IF the operator routes Whisper outputs into AutoGen prompts containing secrets, those secrets can be echoed or summarized.
mitigations: Store sensitive audio in a separate directory from AutoGen workspaces.
Disable network access for AutoGen when processing confidential material.
Redact secrets from transcripts before passing them onward.
Use distinct API keys and accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with OS permissions or containers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has read/write filesystem, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; Whisper is non-networked and non-writing. There is no direct write-write conflict with Whisper, but AutoGen can still contend over shared files if both are pointed at the same audio workspace. The pairwise overlap is therefore a default-unsafe shared-resource risk, though not a high-severity one because Whisper lacks mutable system access.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same working directory, AutoGen can overwrite or rename files Whisper expects.
IF the operator gives AutoGen write access to the audio staging area, file contention can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Make the audio staging directory read-only for AutoGen.
Run AutoGen in a container with a distinct mount namespace.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same transcript filenames.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or a job queue around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or summaries that downstream systems may trust, while Whisper produces transcripts from audio. If Whisper output is fed into AutoGen and then acted on without verification, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect actions. Whisper itself is not an action-taking agent, so the blast radius is limited to downstream misuse rather than direct execution.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative input to AutoGen without human review, transcription mistakes can propagate.
IF AutoGen is allowed to execute code or send messages based on Whisper-derived text, downstream errors can become operational.
mitigations: Require human review of transcripts before AutoGen acts on them.
Add a verification step comparing transcript excerpts to the original audio.
Limit AutoGen to drafting, not executing, when using Whisper output.
Flag low-confidence transcript segments for manual checking.
requires-engineering: add confidence metadata from Whisper into AutoGen’s decision flow.

E_compliance.rationale: Whisper touches audio and speech data, while AutoGen handles application data and model-provider secrets. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated-data certification gap, or retention conflict, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling differences. Because the pair is docs-only and the relevant compliance fields are sparse, uncertainty remains but does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF regulated audio such as PHI is processed through AutoGen without a compliant deployment, compliance risk increases.
IF Whisper transcripts are retained longer than the operator’s policy allows, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify audio inputs before routing them to either agent.
Use a compliant deployment for any regulated data.
Set a short retention window for transcripts and logs.
Separate secrets handling from transcript storage.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
